Author: Ashley Goh Jr.
Review: Yuk Sou Hin has got the best dim sum in Ipoh in my opinion. There are only 2 possible outcomes when you eat their dim sums: a moment of silence as you ruminate over those soothingly delicate morsels or a gasp of amazement by the unexpected …MoreYuk Sou Hin has got the best dim sum in Ipoh in my opinion. There are only 2 possible outcomes when you eat their dim sums: a moment of silence as you ruminate over those soothingly delicate morsels or a gasp of amazement by the unexpected enticing flavours. My experience was a combination of both: the steamed dim sums plumped up with fresh, quality ingredients within the smooth skins made them real delectable, while the familiar taste of the rich molten salted egg custard inside the soft green bun elicited many fond childhood memories of me and my favourite bun. The unconventional skewered pan fried siu mai was utterly luscious, flavourfully coated in a special sweet and savoury brown sauce. Perhaps a rare sighting at yum cha places, but their braised seafood egg noodles topped with large, succulent prawns, scallops and mushrooms are a must order. Cooked to perfection, every strand was marvellously drenched in the piquant, thick gravy that I couldn’t help but mop it clean.

Author: Anastasia Soh
Review: One of A Kind Gastronomical ExperienceAt a glance, RM 675 did seem a little steep for a couple. But when the food …MoreOne of A Kind Gastronomical ExperienceAt a glance, RM 675 did seem a little steep for a couple. But when the food started leaving the kitchen & hitting our table, it was worth every penny. Beautifully presented & nothing short of perfection.The Amuse Bouche arrived literally smoking. A pan seared scallop topped with ossetra caviar accompanied by carrot & cumin sand, crispy duck & finished off with a cress. Just the presentation alone left us wondering what awaited. Once it it entered our mouths, we could only conclude that there was no better way to tease ones palate.Next up was the Foie Gras served on a bed of french brioche & accompanied by caramelised onion puree & grape juice reduction which was soft as a sponge cake & simply melted in our mouths. An absolute treat leaving you craving for more.Mid way, we had an assorted bread basket which were a mixture of store bought & home made delights which were so good that we couldn’t really tell the difference.Up next, the Lobster Bisque with the joy of having the wait staff pouring it table side. It was simply bursting with flavours from the pistachio spheres, corn kernels, lobster dust & poached lobster. It was rich & creamy with a lovely texture to it. We just couldn’t get enough of it!The cod fish arrived beautifully presented & pan fried to perfection, stewed in tomato consommé accompanied by saffron risotto, scallops, mussels & prawns. The Japanese Wagyu Beef was cook perfectly perfectly, medium rare & melted in our mouths. Accompanied with truffle mashed potatoes, burnt onion, porcini mushrooms, charred spring onion & Beef jus.Last but not least, no meal is complete without desserts. An absolutely mouth watering double chocolate accompanied by Ipoh white coffee mousse, pistachio gelato, sea salt, 23k edible gold leaves on a bed of almond crumbs. Absolutely delicious.Our full review is on Instagram (@monk3yseendo)

Author: David Foster
Review: This restaurant is very popular in Ipoh. Advisable to made reservations to avoid disappointment. Always full house. Food served is simply marvellous. Very tasty and delicious. Especially the fried prawns with sauce. Fresh and nice. Steamed chicken with ginger was good 👍.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: M Lee
Review: Vintage banquet style restaurant, the restaurant is so red it's almost blinding, it's like stepping into an alternate universe. Coming to the food, it's very well executed and most importantly clean tasting. They don't over compensate with sauces. Unique touches to what many other places can offer.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Jennifer Lee
Review: A Chinese restaurant with histories, many couples from Ipoh had their wedding receptions here back then. They serve plenty of decent dishes and the one I mugs highlight is their fresh prawns! Juicy, meaty and fragrant which go well on its …MoreA Chinese restaurant with histories, many couples from Ipoh had their wedding receptions here back then. They serve plenty of decent dishes and the one I mugs highlight is their fresh prawns! Juicy, meaty and fragrant which go well on its own or even with some whisky for the night. The interior of the restaurant is typical old Chinese restaurant and most of the staff here are very experienced and well versed with their food menu. Overall good experience of dining here 👍
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Uisge Beatha
Review: Recent lunch with buddies at what’s quite likely Ipoh’s most popular seafood restaurant.   “Pusing Public Seafood Restaurant” (anyone know the history behind such an unusual name?).  Food is really good so no surprise that it’s full most …MoreRecent lunch with buddies at what’s quite likely Ipoh’s most popular seafood restaurant.   “Pusing Public Seafood Restaurant” (anyone know the history behind such an unusual name?).  Food is really good so no surprise that it’s full most lunch and dinners.Fried Cod Fish doused in superior soy sauce.  So so good.  A specialty of the house.Stewed ginger chicken.  A more unusual dish but again, great flavours and texture.Even the humble vegetable was tasty.Deservedly popular.  Highly satisfying meal.@whiskydev
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Hayashi Lim
Review: After read the reviews, we decide went this restaurant for our dinner. We no make a booking but luckily still got table at second floor.Around CNY, they only have menu for CNY Package, or you can order the dish only …MoreAfter read the reviews, we decide went this restaurant for our dinner. We no make a booking but luckily still got table at second floor.Around CNY, they only have menu for CNY Package, or you can order the dish only in the package.All the foods are delicious, especially the prawn, very fresh. The price also reasonable.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Richard_ FoodisLife
Review: There’s very least chance for me to rate a restaurant a 5 stars. This restaurant after so many years dining here still maintain its quality. However the price is on the hike 🙈 Anyway, still very satisfied with its food, and the portion …MoreThere’s very least chance for me to rate a restaurant a 5 stars. This restaurant after so many years dining here still maintain its quality. However the price is on the hike 🙈 Anyway, still very satisfied with its food, and the portion also big. Thumbs up Pusing public👍 So far every of its menu tastes good , personally Would recommend it’s pork tendon specialties. Every time during new year or special occasions I would choose this restaurant.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Kh Wan
Review: Pusing Public never failed us. A must visit for all my Ipoh trips. All their dishes are good and pricing is reasonable. SOP only allowed us to dine-in not more than 7 pax per table so we took 2 tables. Call to make reservations to avoid …MorePusing Public never failed us. A must visit for all my Ipoh trips. All their dishes are good and pricing is reasonable. SOP only allowed us to dine-in not more than 7 pax per table so we took 2 tables. Call to make reservations to avoid disappointment. The "hoi mei poh" (seafood pot) is a personal favourite. The fresh grouper was steamed to perfection.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Jenny Chan
Review: Such a long times didn't came here....still feeling very good and foods also delicious 😉
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Peter Pak

Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Wendy MH
Review: Paid RM95 for the curry chicken bread takeaway for my potluck gathering but the packaging does not even worth 1-star. Looks like street food packaging, not presentable and not hygienic. Using this this kinda plastic bag (refer to pictures).
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Ky
Review: One of the best Chinese restaurant in Ipoh. The food is fresh and delicious with reasonable price. Suitable for family dinner.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Viknesh Govind
Review: Excellent food and service, waiting time could be a little longer due to the crowd,but definitely worth it.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Nicole Nat
Review: Crowded with local and tourist crowd alike. Make your booking first beforehand else you will need to rush your food timing before the next reservation. However very kind of the reception to allow us to dine in right   before the next …MoreCrowded with local and tourist crowd alike. Make your booking first beforehand else you will need to rush your food timing before the next reservation. However very kind of the reception to allow us to dine in right   before the next reservation in 1.5 hours time. We managed to down it in 1 hour. Ordered the famous crabmeat soup, asparagus squid, garoupa fillet and homemade beancurd tofu. Wonderful meal overall. Tummy was too full. Shall revisit.
Location: G 57, 65, Jalan Horley, Kampung Jawa, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Chang Chuntao

Review: Average cafe, with a rustic feel. For example a burger called 'poulet chicken' and items on the specials such as 'Shroomy' which I presume means mushroom, 'monsieur' which translates to 'sir' ...not sure I can eat a man. And a 'tunale'... I have no idea.Food was average, we ordered the 'cheeky panini' and the 'cheeky pizza'. Both were a bit bland in taste and felt a bit let down for the price of the items. The Panini came with a grand total of five crisps.... The pizza didn't really taste like a pizza as all the sections felt like they weren't combining properly. The mint coffee was the best item we ordered.Over all, the food and drinks were okay for what they were, not worth the price though and probably won't be rushing back. The team were friendly enough, even had the little one return our money which was sweet.

The owner is back cooking again and the staff our friendlier and will talk to you as well as joke. Author: 360 Navigate
Review: A small pizzeria in an unassuming yet strategic location, Michaelangelo's Pizzeria is an Ipoh favourite but probably doesn't get highlighted much as a local specialty due to its Western nature. Being in a somewhat minority by serving pork, …MoreA small pizzeria in an unassuming yet strategic location, Michaelangelo's Pizzeria is an Ipoh favourite but probably doesn't get highlighted much as a local specialty due to its Western nature. Being in a somewhat minority by serving pork, that's played a big part in its reputation for the best pork pizza in town. That might not say a lot, but it probably ranks high amongst other eatieries in the Klang Valley that offer anything similar.Hog Extreme, the meat lovers pizza full of varied pork ingredients is arguably the house favourite for locals and tourists alike. There are plenty of others as well, with the menu being generally varied, with some pasta options as well for those who don't feel like having a slice.Operating everyday (except Monday) from 6:30 - 10:30 PM, opportunities to dine in are limited in a place that squeezes probably 50 persons at any one time. As a result, many are content to order takeouts as well.The shoplot they're currently operating in is the same as when they started, which is somewhat narrow, and the feel of dining is probably the same as myBurgerLab in SS2. It's naturally noisy with the crowd, but some may find the loud background music is an unecessary addition to the already loud atmosphere.That said, customer service is generally good. They are usually in a hurry due to the high turnover of clientele, but manage to be generally polite and efficient more often that not.
Location: No. 40, Jln Medan Ipoh 1B, Medan Ipoh Bestari, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Kah Soon Ang
Review: Pizza - I know I will go for Pizza Hut when I am in Ipoh, but knowing a Michelangelo's Pizzeria in Ipoh is quite a surprise to me, more so that it is operated by a Westerner. No long list of food greets you in Michelangelo's Pizzeria's …MorePizza - I know I will go for Pizza Hut when I am in Ipoh, but knowing a Michelangelo's Pizzeria in Ipoh is quite a surprise to me, more so that it is operated by a Westerner. No long list of food greets you in Michelangelo's Pizzeria's menu, but I was still a little taken aback from the offered choices. Don't expect to see your familiar combinations from Pizza Hut. I took quite some time to go through all the names, and if not for the explanations underneath each name, I think I will be spending half an hour asking the waiter/waitress to know what I want.The waiters and waitresses go through their job with an energy and friendliness that make me long for Michelangelo's Pizzeria. Truly, such attitude is missing from current waiters and waitresses serving in the food franchise industry.If this is America in winter, I would expect the place to be warm and cozy. The owner brought exactly that kind of feel to local soil when he set up the place. Warm greeting, warm amber lighting on yellow painted walls, along with portraits of American culture hanging on the wall makes you forget that you are on Malaysian soil. I am not particularly impressed by the rock (or was it pop...?) song running through the speakers, but that was me. Don't let my personal disinterest for songs undermine the environment.You can get a full pizza at the offered flavor, or you could choose to have half of the pizza at one flavor, another half at another flavor, which is how most people like to order. You will be paying for half the price of a full pizza for that flavor if you opted for the latter method, so you get to taste more types of flavor. At my friends' behest, we opted for Blue Cheese, Bacon and Eggs (isn't that like an English breakfast?), Salami Special, and The Hog (sounds like some monstrosity).Of course Michelangelo's Pizzeria isn't just about pizzas, despite its name. You can't get away with pastas when it comes to Italian food, and so pasta it is! The Garden Spaghetti that was served up appeared to be quite a huge portion, but fortunately we had more than a few hungry stomachs to fill. If you ordered for pizza and not everyone is ready for second round, then better leave this be, and get it on your next visit.You ain't been to Michelangelo's Pizzeria if you ain't tried their cheesecake balls. Trust me, they worth every dollar and penny (or RM and cents in our case) in your pocket. These balls of cheesecake are larger than your average chicken eggs, and comes in either almond coated or Oreo coated.
Location: No. 40, Jln Medan Ipoh 1B, Medan Ipoh Bestari, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Ashley Goh Jr.
Review: I never knew this place existed until I googled for good food places in Ipoh. Seeing the high ratings quickly got me on the phone making a reservation. The restaurant gave me an impression of a circus with its red and yellow theme colour . …MoreI never knew this place existed until I googled for good food places in Ipoh. Seeing the high ratings quickly got me on the phone making a reservation. The restaurant gave me an impression of a circus with its red and yellow theme colour .Two things I knew I wanted to order for certain before I arrived, were their highly raved Char Siew and steamed lala. The gloriously glazed Char Siew were thickly sliced and had a good fat to lean meat ratio. The luscious Char Siew was marinated in the right sauce and barbecued to perfection; rendering such tender and succulent meat that stood up to my high expectations. The steamed Lala was truly sublime, where my senses were instantly awaken as I took my first sip of the exceptionally fragrant broth that was saturated by the sweetness of the remarkably fresh and plump Lala. The aromatic stingray curry had a pleasant pungent flavour that wasn’t too heavy nor light, thick nor watery and had the perfect level of spiciness. It is my first time ordering steamed egg prawns and it turned out silky-licious despite its unassuming appearance. Even the vegetable was wonderfully cooked, yielding a soft yet crunchy texture.Every dish at The Museum was perfectly cooked and boasted with immense freshness. I’ll definitely be back to try that and their other dishes after such an excellent experience.

Author: Uisge Beatha
Review: The second of my 2 must eats when in Ipoh is a visit to Tuck Kee.  My thoughts…1) There is a branch in Damansara Uptown that’s frankly a poor copy of the …MoreThe second of my 2 must eats when in Ipoh is a visit to Tuck Kee.  My thoughts…1) There is a branch in Damansara Uptown that’s frankly a poor copy of the original.  There is also a Tuck Kee Son (naturally run by the son) in Singapore that offers quite tasty food but the taste of their famous “Yit Kong Hor” (Moonlight Rice Noodles) is a little different.  Think it’s down to the sauces used.2) So Tuck Kee in Ipoh is still a pretty unique taste experience.  Many rave and come for their “Yit Kong Hor” which is Hokkien style fried rice noodles topped with a raw egg.  Hokkien style means the use of dark soy sauce and the topped egg when mixed into the noodles gives it a lovely creamy texture.  (The yellow egg yolk juxtaposed against the dark noodles background is the reason for the moonlight moniker).  Unfortunately, I personally think this dish is over rated.  It’s good but somewhat boring.3) Noodles wise, I prefer the “Yin Yong”.  Cantonese fried noodles with a crispy fried vermicelli paired with wok singed rice noodles.  The noodles are topped with an egg based sauce.  No dark soy with Cantonese style cooking.  Tuck Kee’s version is so very yummy.4) My favourite dish is the blanched baby octopus in a superior light soy sauce.  Delightful with or without the accompanying chili sauce.  It’s the soy based sauce that once again provides the magic (as per Onn Kee’s Chicken).  Could eat this every week! ❤️😊Overall, I’m still a big fan of the original Tuck Kee restaurant in Ipoh. Good stuff! 😊@whiskydev
Restaurant: Ipoh Tuck Kee Restaurant 德记炒粉专门店
Location: 61, Jalan Yau Tet Shin, Taman Jubilee, Ipoh, Perak

Moving “oolong”, I settled upon their Black Tea Chicken Curry, braised Beef Brisket in Black Tea served with green tea rice and a pair of their housemade buns. Author: Brandon Lim
Review: Easily the best meal I've had so far in Malaysia! The entire menu at Purple Cane Tea House features Hakka style cuisine that incorporates tea in its ingredients. I've never tasted cuisine that utilizes tea in it's recipes which expertly …MoreEasily the best meal I've had so far in Malaysia! The entire menu at Purple Cane Tea House features Hakka style cuisine that incorporates tea in its ingredients. I've never tasted cuisine that utilizes tea in it's recipes which expertly elevated the flavors of each dish we ordered. Not everything pictured is vegan as I was the only veg head amongst my lunch companions but the menu had an impressive amount of vegan & vegetarian fare. Highlights included:*Stir Fried Abalone Mushroom with Dried Chili and Lychee Black Tea Sauce, a vegan take on a popular dish here that normally uses battered Mantis Shrimp. The sauce was slightly sweet with a savory tanginess.*Lion's Mane Mushroom in a sweet & sour sauce infused with Oolong Tea. This one seemed to be a vegan take on the popular Western Chinese favorite Sweet and Sour Pork. My friends said that they wouldn't have been able to tell it was not meat if they weren't told so. Happy to see a restaurant that does not rely on predictable processed soy and gluten proteins to achieve it's faux meat substitutes. I wish more vegan restaurants in the West would catch onto this but perhaps it's not as economical as soy is so overproduced in N America.*Braised Bean Curd in Tea Sauce was a dome shaped mound of silky fried tofu topped with diced mushroom and carrots in a cornstarch heavy sauce that also used Oolong which is a naturally sweet and fragrant tea.The tea cups look like they have Matcha in them but it's actually a rich and robust tasting soup made from Fennel puree and a variety of teas. The Mantou fried sweet bread was meant to be dipped into it. I couldn't believe the bread was deep fried as it was so light and fluffy and not oily or crispy at all. Apparently the key to achieving this texture is by using a very high temperature for the oil it's fried in.After the meal one of the supervisors Peggy hosted a very lovely and informative tea ceremony for us. She was very charming and knowledgable thank you Peggy!I certainly walked away from this meal feeling incredibly full, content, and inspired.
Location: 2, Jalan Dato Tahwil Azhar, Osbrone Street, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Dr. Samy Velu Chandrasagaran
Review: The food was delicious. But I still doubt whether it justifies the price. I walked in knowing the price but still somewhat find the food is average. The reason why I gave 3 star was 2 things; …MoreThe food was delicious. But I still doubt whether it justifies the price. I walked in knowing the price but still somewhat find the food is average. The reason why I gave 3 star was 2 things;1. The table concept. We booked for 10people seating and the table was very wide, literally. And it was very difficult to pass each other the food we ordered from one corner to the other as I have to stand each time to pass food to my siblings or my mom. I've sat in restaurants with more family members and we were given beautiful round table with centre setting that can spin for easy reach.2. I booked table from 7pm to 7.30pm and I arrived at 7pm and ordered shortly after. My sibling arrived at 7.45pm. We were only informed at restaurant that the table that we sat has another reservation at 8.30pm. which I find very unpleasant. I should have been informed that when I call to make reservation. The reason why I do family dinners during holidays is to catch up with family and relatives and normally will sit for at least 2hrs. I find it not pleasant as I paid close to RM500 for the dinner.Pls take note. Tq.

Author: Andrew Phang
Review: The setup and decor of this restaurant was nice. It was a quiet, comfortable restaurant with a soft music playing in the back. The prices of the food were reasonable, however one peculiar thing are the famous teas here. You have to order by …MoreThe setup and decor of this restaurant was nice. It was a quiet, comfortable restaurant with a soft music playing in the back. The prices of the food were reasonable, however one peculiar thing are the famous teas here. You have to order by the pot but no refill services are provided. (Basically you are ordering 2 small tea cups lo.) I ordered the lamb - RM88, and their famous tea smoked chicken - RM25.FIrst the chicken, if you have experience buying chicken from wet market and big malls, you know the most significant difference is the freshness. There is a certain smell from the chicken if its not fresh. Although the tea smoked chicken came with a lovely tea sauce, the funky smell especially around the bone area was quite unpleasant.Secondly the lamb rack. I ordered it to be cooked medium. I received it with a smile as the decor of the plate was nice. However, the first thing i notice is the cuts of the lamb were odd. although the portion was reasonable, one chuck of it has one rack bone, 2 of them has 2 rack bone. If all the sizes are not the same, it means the oven cooking technique will not be the same on all pieces. The funny thing is, ALL pieces came out RAW. If they were medium well, or medium rare (one rank above or below medium), I can accept it, but raw? Come on dude. There were still white fat that were present and it means it wasn't rendered enough.Told the waiter about it, and he was very apologetic. Took back the plate of lamb, and I was a bit surprised they didn't recook another plate but took the original ones, put it in the oven, dump a huge amount of sauce on it and serve it back. Anyone who knows how to cook a steak/lamb knows that's not the way dude. Do take note that the restaurant has uncertain opening hours (usually from 6pm to 930pm) do check first before you visit to avoid disappointment.Do take note also that this is NOT a chicken 🐔 rice ship (they don't serve rice). Anyway, we ordered one whole chicken 5 🌟, a plate of bean sprouts 5 🌟 (always a must!), and another signature chicken feet 5 🌟, and a few bowls of hor fun 5 🌟. Plus drink... For a table of 4 the bill came out to be RM105 which was a bit pricey for Ipoh standard.The food here especially the Signature chicken was cooked to perfection....  smooth, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The bean sprouts here is ipoh styled (short and fat) which goes really well with the chicken and Hor Fun. The chicken feet (Phoenix Claw) here was so good that even when I don't usually eat chicken feet.. I had a few bites.Being a favourite since I was a kid, I love the hot fun texture and the Taugeh crunchiness... which was cooked to perfection. However I had comments from my other friends that the meat was a bit salty and maybe too raw (you will see slight blood on the chicken meat) and also some comments that it's too oily. Depending on your taste buds... I believe this place is not for everyone... As I am of the opinion that this is the best chicken Taugeh place in all of Ipoh and probably Malaysia.Taste Rating 10/10Ambience Rating 6/10Service Rating 7/10Value Rating 8/10

Author: Deborah Yaw
Review: No more next time ever. A disgrace to the Ipoh f&b scene. Ruined what could’ve been a good dinner to end the year. …MoreNo more next time ever. A disgrace to the Ipoh f&b scene. Ruined what could’ve been a good dinner to end the year.Everytime I come here, I always seem to forget how impeccably obnoxious and over the top the service is - how you can wait for over an hour to be served your appetisers and soup, and wait another half hour for the mains and then wait some more to pay at the counter.The 10% service charge is to hear them apologise over and over throughout your meal, and to never have your water refilled when you’re parched beyond waiting. I came in with no expectations only to have my meal ruined by a place where I had to demand for my food and I was even as desperate to willingly cancel my mains and walk out the door only to be told to wait a little while more to be served.The only saving grace was my steak actually  came medium rare and the lamb shank still tasted the same as we had it 2 years back before the MCO (mind you, I was reminded again that service was also at snail pace back then). I feel sorry for the kitchen staff to be working with such terrible service team.What was even more disappointing was how we were being served a lot later than tables that came way after we arrived and made our order - which goes to show how messy their service line is.Please save yourself some time and go to better places to deservingly have a good meal. This place has gone to the gutter for me.
Location: Taman Desa Tambun Indah, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Benjamin Bromberg
Review: We had a decent meal with good service at citrus. The pricing is definitely above average and that resembles in a nice environment for half the restaurant and the other half with wooden chairs and mamak style tables. A very weird mix. …MoreWe had a decent meal with good service at citrus. The pricing is definitely above average and that resembles in a nice environment for half the restaurant and the other half with wooden chairs and mamak style tables. A very weird mix.However the food presentation is good and the quality somewhere between very good and average. The bruschetta came with the tomato mix on the side, I have never gotten it anywhere else than on the bread before. My lamb 3 way was 2 way ok and 1 way tasty. The desert was quite nice and I really liked the combination of chocolate and fruits.However the Mojito came with no noticeable alcohol and I had to ask them to check if they forgot to put any in, they took back the drink and brought it out later with alcohol inside the same glass. For a place that aims to be upper class and charges accordingly I would expect to redo it properly.All in all the food can be nice, the service friendly but not very polished. The place has potential but doesn’t quite justify the price for the experience we had.
Location: Taman Desa Tambun Indah, Ipoh, Perak

Author: Carson Lee
Review: I was looking for a nice French restaurant in Ipoh to bring my girlfriend to when I was told about Having's by my sister. The chef is a very passionate man of his craft, with years of experience in Michelin starred restaurants in France and …MoreI was looking for a nice French restaurant in Ipoh to bring my girlfriend to when I was told about Having's by my sister. The chef is a very passionate man of his craft, with years of experience in Michelin starred restaurants in France and London.My sister contacted them for me since the owner is an acquaintance of her. Knowing how I was allergic to seafood, they came up with a special menu just for us.They even provided us with a wine recommendation (you have to bring your own because they do not sell wine).It was a scrumptious 6 course meal that started with a sweet potato and lemongrass soup. The sunflower seeds in the creamy soup gave it a very interesting texture.For the appetizer, we were served a duo of salmon rillettes & gravlax. Coming back from Japan, I was not expecting to be impressed by the salmon but I was gladly proved wrong.Moving on to the 3rd, we had foie gras cooked 2 ways, with pear jam and brioche. This was the first time I ever had foie gras and it tasted absolutely amazing. Paired with the jam and brioche, I cleaned up the plate in no time.The 4th course was blueberry sorbet & vodka. The acidic taste of the blueberry helped open up my appetite for the main as I was already a little stuffed from the previous courses.We had a short break before being served the main course of herb-crusted rack of lamb, ratatouille, and pommes fondant. The lamb was cooked to medium as recommended and the meat had just the right amount of give to it. I also enjoyed the pommes fondant a lot, with its soft inner core and chewy exterior.The fantastic meal was ended with chocolate fondant and Bailey's ice cream. It wasn't too sweet, which is just the way I like it, and the chocolate was very rich.Our waiting staff was very friendly and alert. My wine glass was almost never empty.The price for such an amazing experience was very fair.I highly recommended Having's to anyone in Ipoh looking for some wonderful French food.
Location: 8, Pusat Perdagangan Canning 3, Pusat Perdagangan, Lorong Canning, Ipoh

Author: Steven Naeyaert
Review: We had a strange experience in Vnam Kitchen. The restaurant was less than half full however the staff looked extremely busy and frantic. The food (pho bo and papaya salad) was ok, not great. Flavours were definitely recognizable of …MoreWe had a strange experience in Vnam Kitchen. The restaurant was less than half full however the staff looked extremely busy and frantic. The food (pho bo and papaya salad) was ok, not great. Flavours were definitely recognizable of Vietnamese food though not the same as the real thing in Vietnam (which is to be expected in Malaysia). Most of the staff were friendly with exception of someone who kept messing with my Vietnamese dripping coffee. It was clear it was badly set up in the beginning and she kept trying to fix it. Coming back a couple of times to the table without saying anything and just starting to mess with it, it was weird. One of the times she asked a question in a rude manner. When we kindly replied she didn't seem to believe us than refuted what we said and walked away. It was so strange and shocking I started to laugh. The next time she came back to mess with the coffee I kindly said to her that it was ok and that she should just let it be, that we've been to Vietnam before and even make Vietnamese dripping coffee at home. She again looked at us in disbelief and walked away, she didn't return though. 😀 The coffee ended up below average. Maybe just a bad day!?Prices are high for what you get in Malaysia and a lot more than in Vietnam.

Location: 32, Jalan Seenivasagam, Ipoh, Perak

Located in Menglembu, this eatery is a gem as not many outsiders know of it's existence and confined only to mostly locals. …MoreOne of the best, if not the best, Chinese restaurants in Ipoh. Located in Menglembu, this eatery is a gem as not many outsiders know of it's existence and confined only to mostly locals.Their signature dishes are on par or better than other Chinese restaurants in Ipoh. The dishes are:a) Fried big prawns with their special soy sauce. The dish is separated with the body being served in halves and the head is braised and cooked with yee mee.b) Crab soup cooked with bitter gourd and served with koay teow noodles. The crab is nice and the soup is delicious.c) Braised giant garoupa with yam. This is definitely one of the best I ever had. Recommended.d) Ask the captain to recommend other signature dishes as the above is good enough to fill up for 10 persons.Price is about RM100 per head for above dishes. Food is good and there's ample parking in the front of the restaurant. Enjoy the new gem in Ipoh.

We were super disgusted with the service. Overall was not a pleasant coffee & desserts treat for us. Author: Tony Z
Review: A Vegan restaurant with a good range of menu of Western, Oriental and Local dishes. The dishes are apparently mainly plant based with minimal gluten and not much flour based menu varieties compared to the normal main streamed vegetarian …MoreA Vegan restaurant with a good range of menu of Western, Oriental and Local dishes. The dishes are apparently mainly plant based with minimal gluten and not much flour based menu varieties compared to the normal main streamed vegetarian restaurants. Probably this is a good restaurant choice for people who avoid gluten and wheats products. However, be aware this restaurant has not declared it is gluten free.The food here are surprisingly flavourful and delicious although it is a vegan plant based restaurant establishment. If you have not tried Vegan food and think eating vegetables and just plants is not palatable, come and try and it may surprised you!The one thing I did not like about this place  is that the sauces offered here are are a tad too sweet to be consider as healthy. Though the food here are not salty but on the converse very sweet. The reprieve is that fortunately the sauces come separately so you can use sparingly. I would prefer if there is an option for less sweet sauces or even diabetic friendly sauces. Veganism is not only about against animal cruelty but as importantly wholesome plant based healthy food, low salty, sugars and oils. Hopefully the management will take note and provide alternatives for health conscious diners and put a great importance to healthy eating and avoid MSG, artificial colourings, good conditioners and preservatives, too.This is the first time I tried Vegan cakes. I can say that it is as good as the real deal. Go and try it yourself, the proof is in the pudding. Tried blueberry and cheese cake, it is as if it is the real thing! I would be suspecting that it cannot be Vegan but I believe the proprietor is honest and a Vegan himself.This is one of the rare vegan restaurants that one can find in Ipoh City. According to the restaurant, nothing that is of animal product or animal origins are used as a ingredients in the food served here. So you won't get any milk, butter or egg and even honey in your food here. If one is a truly animal lover, eating vegan good, this is the place you can dine with a conscience. Ipoh City seemed to be joining the global trends of animal rights and anti animal cruelty with the sprouting of vegan restaurants lately.The place is run by mainly staff with some disabilities. Be aware that the servers do not looked like they have a disabilities as they do not verbally greet you as they have speech disabilities. So may need to use sign language or gestures to communicate.However, this restaurant is a self ordering so you need to select your meals, write and fill in your food orders and go to the counter to order and pay. In this way, any ordering difficulties and mistakes can be avoided and overcome since the servers are indisposed to take orders effectively. This work around allows this restaurant to employ the diasbled and should be lauded. Hats off to the owners to give the disabled an opportunity to work and be financially independent.A good place to eat a healthy plant based diet and at the same time support the disabled community if you dining in this venue and contribution to patronising good social responsible businesses set up that support the under privileged community.
Location: No. 12, Jalan Raja Permaisuri Bainun, Ipoh, Perak

Review: Sin Lean Lee (新联利) restaurant. A highly recommended coffee shop in Old Town, Ipoh to take your breakfast due to its variety and quality of food. To name a few: chee cheong fun, Penang laksa, toasted bread, etc. Always on my mind is to order …MoreSin Lean Lee (新联利) restaurant. A highly recommended coffee shop in Old Town, Ipoh to take your breakfast due to its variety and quality of food. To name a few: chee cheong fun, Penang laksa, toasted bread, etc. Always on my mind is to order fried kway teow. This stall, obviously the most popular here, has a unique way of stir-frying to produce a moist, slimy variation. Another stall serves aromatic glutinous rice with sweet kaya. Too bad they don't take the trouble to colour the rice blue with butterfly-pea flower. The coffee and Chinese tea brewed here are good enough to complement your breakfast. As dessert, get some egg tarts (original as well as pandan flavour) as takeaway from Egg Tarts King stall (All Inn Café) just across the road.Updates: Sin Lean Lee (新联利) restaurant has now shifted to another nearby location. Its old corner premise is now managed by Kin Kok (建国) coffee shop after a major renovation. The popular fried kway teow stall now operates in Kin Kok. The Egg Tarts King stall has shifted to Kin Kok too.
Location: 15, Jalan Panglima, Ipoh, Perak

Although leaning towards the drier side, the remarkable punch of flavours together with the chunky lentil curry made it a splendid dish.Bursting with intense, tantalising flavours and cooked to a perfect firmness but not al dente since it’s a term only used for dry pastas, find every strand thoroughly coated with the savoury, spicy hot relish.The flavours doesn’t stop there as the enticing variety of mojitos were all incredibly refreshing too.

Author: Ken Tan
Review: Visited this place on 2nd November 2018. It was a public holiday for Perak. The dim sum most of them were handmade and fresh. Would specially recommend their Lau sar pau. It has lotus paste in it. So, the taste would not be too salty and …MoreVisited this place on 2nd November 2018. It was a public holiday for Perak. The dim sum most of them were handmade and fresh. Would specially recommend their Lau sar pau. It has lotus paste in it. So, the taste would not be too salty and oily. The presence of the lotus paste has balanced the salty taste from the salty egg. To my surprise, most of the pau here were not oily and has the fluffy texture. Besides that, I will like to recommend the groundnut soup. It has the silky and soft texture with fine sweetness. Apart from that, the prawns used in some of the dim sum is relatively fresh. You can taste the chewiness of the prawn. For ambience wise, try to go around 8 to 9am, or in the morning to avoid the crowd. You can definitely see a lot locals here as well.  In term of price, it was quite reasonable. This place has surely earned my next visit.
Location: 57-59, Jalan Raja Ekram, Ipoh, Perak

Author: DR. ALVIN TUNG
Review: Surprisingly, this was only my first visit having driven past this famous restaurant for many years. Not always my fault though because with the best of intentions, many times it was closed or sold out! But this morning they were open for …MoreSurprisingly, this was only my first visit having driven past this famous restaurant for many years. Not always my fault though because with the best of intentions, many times it was closed or sold out! But this morning they were open for business and I had an opportunity to sample their famous Hakka mee.The dish arrived in three separate bowls with one containing a fried tofu wrapper with taro and water chestnut, then another bowl with soup containing stuffed tofu, meatballs and fish balls and finally, the main bowl of noodles with a generous amount of fried minced pork on top. Once you add a scoop or two of soup and mix up the noodles, it makes for an incredibly delicious dish, with very flavourful minced pork and al dente noodles. The accompanying meatballs and tofu were also very tasty especially when dipped in their homemade chili sauce making for a well balanced meal. Not to be overlooked but their kopi was also very tasty. It was rich and flavorful. All COVID protocols and best practices were strictly observed by all. A great breakfast all in all. Remember to show up early to avoid disappointment as they ALWAYS sell out!
Location: 190, Jalan Sultan Iskandar, Taman Jubilee, Ipoh, Perak

Review: K Ten is synonymous with claypot chicken rice (瓦煲鸡饭) in Ipoh. Main one in Bercham and a sub in Medan Ipoh. I have patronised this K Ten (Medan Ipoh) quite a number of times. Every time we look forward to a claypot of steaming fragrant …MoreK Ten is synonymous with claypot chicken rice (瓦煲鸡饭) in Ipoh. Main one in Bercham and a sub in Medan Ipoh. I have patronised this K Ten (Medan Ipoh) quite a number of times. Every time we look forward to a claypot of steaming fragrant chicken rice with side dishes like delicious braised chicken feet and crunchy green vegetables. The chicken feet are cooked to the right munchy texture. The chicken meat mixed with the rice are well marinated. Thumbs-up for the quality! Eh, eat all this with a bit of the chili padi in soy sauce. Blends well with the food with added satisfaction. Suggest a pot of hot Chinese tea to complement the meal. There are other cuisine like steamed fish, curry fish head or smaller side dishes like fish balls or tofu stuff. But people usually go for the main specialty. Compare the food here with the one in Bercham. My rating: just as good! Parking here is not a problem unlike that in Bercham. To tell the truth, Kampar is the town for food lovers hunting for even better serving of this style of cooking chicken rice.
Location: 57, Jalan Medan Ipoh 2, Bandar Baru Medan Ipoh, Ipoh, Perak

He went to check in the kitchen and insisted that it was freshly cooked and has no any sign of spoilage, and he guaranteed us that it is good to go and it’s edible. Being a foodie person, I’m know what I’m having, as I’ve been professionally trained in culinary field.Despite all mentioned above, I was also being charged accordingly, which I’ve no problem in paying it, however, as a return guest, to encounter such experience without any service recovery, I would say you have lost another return customer. Being said, we all eat, and it would be a sad waste of opportunity to eat badly.If you don’t mind me sharing some tips, it would be best if you are able to taste your food from time to time, and communicate more with guest by asking feedback, practice service recovery if needed, for example, offered the guest an alternative in food selection or a free meal and all this had to done by the person in charged to maximize its effect, what’s more when you can convert a dissatisfied customer to return customer.I sincerely hope the above can be change, even a “Yucky” foods deserve a second tasting, I hope the next time will be a better dining experience for me and my family.

Author: Jim Lau
Review: Type: Chinese CafeSignature: Dim Sum and White Coffee …MoreType: Chinese CafeSignature: Dim Sum and White CoffeeVisited A Jie Cafe at an odd hour of 345pm with 9 people.... The manager gave us a large table and we started ordering what's left (available food in the menu).As a rundown, we ordered their signature A Jie White Coffee (ice and hot) 4.5 🌟 which was really good. Then we ordered 2 bowls of Assam Laksa 4 🌟 .. Thick and nice but my only complain is that it doesn't come with chunky fish. The Toast with Kaya 4 🌟 was also nice but one friend commented that it didnt come with butter... So immedietly the staff brought butter (upon request).. That's great customer service.In addition, we ordered Char Siew Pao (BBQ Pork Bun) 5 🌟 and this was really big and nice. This is unlike normal ones as the meat is juicy and the portion (size) is huge. We also tried the Bread with Chicken Curry 3.5 🌟 and the Braised Pork Rice 4 🌟. The one I personally like the most is actually the Rojak 5 🌟 which comes with thick and delicious sauce... And it even comes with a small plate of spicy chili if in case you want to spice up the Rojak. Very thoughtful indeed!Generally, everyone here enjoyed the food and we will definitely be back the next time we are around the corner. Since this round, a lot of their signature was sold out.. We will definitely try those during our next visit.Taste Rating 9/10Ambience Rating 8/10Service Rating 9/10Value Rating 8/10

Author: DR. ALVIN TUNG
Review: Fabulous hidden cafe! Came on the recommendation of friends. Doesn't even have a sign or front but filled to capacity with regulars! They have many signature dishes. We tried the longan tau fu fa, Guilin gao, white coffee, kueh, Nasi …MoreFabulous hidden cafe! Came on the recommendation of friends. Doesn't even have a sign or front but filled to capacity with regulars! They have many signature dishes. We tried the longan tau fu fa, Guilin gao, white coffee, kueh, Nasi kerabu, Tom yum bee hon, Assam Laksa and all of them were absolutely delicious. For sure we will be back! The decor inside is also very charming with a rack of old time coffee cups and the decor is very nostalgic and adds to the atmosphere. The A/C especially on a hot day is a welcome luxury! The boss lady is very inviting and charismatic. Very attentive to her guests and makes them feel at home.After a two-year hiatus due to the pandemic, our first visit did not disappoint in the slightest! In fact, everything tasted even BETTER than we remembered! It was like meeting up with an old friend! Texture was smooth and rich. Coffee is full-bodied but not overbearing and pleasantly sweet. Best white coffee I have had this trip so far! Friendly courteous hard working staff observed COVID protocols and best practices. One of our favourite spots to eat!
Location: 61, Persiaran Tokong, Taman Hoover, Ipoh, Perak

In 1989, a person named Jiang Yongqiang on the Daheyuan Street in Ipoh opened a “Changjiang Tea Room”, which was also used as a store and wholesale. First, the roasted white coffee was sold to other tea houses in Ipoh. The market responded well. Their confidence grew & sales improved significantly .. so, in order to continue the culture of his father, Jiang Yongqiang white coffee, Jiang Xiujie, his second-generation daughter, who often went to her father's tea room as a helper during her studies,  continued to learn the white coffee brewing method .. over time, Jiang Xiujie mastered the secret of brewing white coffee. The unique formula and brewing method make the white coffee more mellow, so the “Changjiang Tea Room” quickly became famous all over Ipoh. Jiang Xiujie renamed the original store “Changjiang Tea Room” to “Jiangshi White Coffee Tea Room” and continued to operate. In order to enhance the brand culture of the original "Jiang's White Coffee", the concept of a unique Nanyang style Jié Cafe [Ajie Jiang's White Coffee Teahouse] was established. This Jié Cafe [Ajie Jiang's White Coffee Teahouse] was established mainly to cater to the unique taste tt resulted fr their white coffee brewing method. In addition to enhancing the cultural orientation of the “Jiang's White Coffee” brand, this café also displays the old furniture, "chicken bowl" tableware & famous calligraphy that Yibao passed onto the current generation. Every corner of the cafe tells a story.A Jié Cafe [Ajie Jiang's White Coffee Teahouse]APRIL 1, 2018Address: 61, Persiaran Tokong, Ipoh, Perak 31650Business Hours: 9:30 AM - 5:00 PM

Review: 362 Gunung Rapat 崑崙喇叭炭燒香餅. Watching the entire round of heong peng making. Reminiscing the old time when I used to stay and work in Ipoh. …More362 Gunung Rapat 崑崙喇叭炭燒香餅. Modern machine and traditional charcoal burnt made. Master Liow made a step further back in time, coconut husks as charcoal fuel in fiery hot furnace. Among the last one standing to do so. Exceeding all heong peng standard, by using premium lards only, not vegetables oil or margarine. Each one handcrafted with love and care from his own hand.He was one of the earliest and directly trained from young by Yee Hup founder to rise up in rank as their chief baker. Before parting ways to start on his own when Master Liow preferred to do what he did best and been doing so philosophically. The legacy, cultural heritage and history of heong peng making, all in one humble place.Whenever, you give me a heong peng and say it's good. I'll just show you happy face, because I know you probably haven't seen a real traditional heong peng and how it was made.

Author: Jimmy Chan
Review: An unexpected  village house that is actually a Traditional Hong Peah bakery. On the outside it looks just like another village/kampung house but once you stepped in you see a couple churning out dough, rolling and patting with force and …MoreAn unexpected  village house that is actually a Traditional Hong Peah bakery. On the outside it looks just like another village/kampung house but once you stepped in you see a couple churning out dough, rolling and patting with force and arranging it in an organised honeycomb pattern. They use a Earthen kiln like those of a Tandoor but this is more solid plus thicker and coconut husk is used for the fire. Just by placing your hand above it you can feel the heat coming up like a volcano. And with that when its hot enough you see the tradition in action, is like a nice Baking Dance where the man go round sprinkling water follow-by placing raw Hong Peah into the hot Kiln, try imagine your hand getting baked, that's how it feels each time he puts each Hong Peah. The Hong Peah is crispy & flaky and thick, in it's crust is a thin layer of caramel. Their Jong Peah get sold off fast daily. Parking (by the road side) is limited here.
